title: Internal Hom from a finite free sheaf is exact
statement: Let $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be a site with a sheaf of commutative rings (a ringed site) [def-pur-sheaf-hom], let $E$ be an $\mathcal O_U$-module equipped with an isomorphism $E\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ for some integer $r\geq0$, and let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $0\to\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E,A)\to\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E,B)\to\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E,C)\to0$ is exact; under the chosen isomorphism $E\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$, each internal Hom is canonically identified with the corresponding direct sum $A^{\oplus r}$, $B^{\oplus r}$, or $C^{\oplus r}$.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 (Lemma 20.51.4, case (2)), finite locally free Hom calculation in the proof

proof.text: Use the chosen isomorphism E|_V \cong O_V^{\oplus r} on every object V of the site. By the definition of sheaf Hom, restriction to V gives Hom_{O|_V}(E|_V,A|_V), and precomposition with this isomorphism identifies it naturally with Hom_{O|_V}(O_V^{\oplus r},A|_V) \cong A(V)^{\oplus r}. The same construction applies to B and C and is compatible with restriction maps, so it gives sheaf isomorphisms Hom(E,A) \cong A^{\oplus r}, Hom(E,B) \cong B^{\oplus r}, and Hom(E,C) \cong C^{\oplus r}.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 (Lemma 20.51.4), case (2), finite locally free Hom calculation

proof.text: Under these identifications, the maps induced by A \to B \to C are the r-fold direct sums of the given maps, because the sheaf-Hom maps act by postcomposition and the identifications use the r coordinate inclusions and projections. The category of sheaves of O-modules is abelian, so kernels and cokernels are computed in that category; finite direct sums are computed coordinatewise. Therefore the direct-sum sequence 0 \to A^{\oplus r} \to B^{\oplus r} \to C^{\oplus r} \to 0 is exact, including r = 0.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 (Lemma 20.51.4), case (2), exactness after finite locally free Hom identification

proof.text: The three sheaf isomorphisms constructed in Step 1 form a commutative diagram from the direct-sum sequence in Step 2 to the displayed internal-Hom sequence, because each vertical map is precomposition with the same chosen isomorphism E \cong O_U^{\oplus r} and each horizontal map is postcomposition by A \to B or B \to C. Thus the internal-Hom sequence has the same sectionwise kernels and locally surjective epimorphism as the exact direct-sum sequence, and the three vertical maps give the claimed identifications.
